records.title: Director, Operations Program Management
records.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 Agility Robotics is scaling its operations — and the programs that enable that scale need to be led with rigor, depth, and autonomy. As Director, Operations Program Management, you will own two things simultaneously: a team of technical and non-technical program managers working across all of the operations and supply chain domains and a portfolio of high-complexity programs that span the full organization. 

 Reporting to the Sr. Director of Operations Program Management & Insights, you will bring the structure, judgment, and leadership presence to operate with minimal oversight. You set the standard for what great program management looks like on this team. 

 This is the right role for someone who leads from the front, develops the people around them, and can drive complex cross-functional programs to outcomes without being told how to get there. 

 About the Work 

 
 Lead and develop a team of dedicated program managers. Set clear expectations, coach toward growth, and hold yourself accountable to building a stronger team over time. 

 Establish and model PM best practices across the team. You are both the standard-setter and the coach. 

 Own, through your and the team’s efforts, a portfolio of complex programs that require a high degree of structure, judgment, and organizational reach. Act as a player-coach on the team’s broader portfolio — holding your own programs while helping your direct reports navigate blockers and deliver against theirs. 

 Translate complex, multi-org work into clear progress narratives for executive audiences. You know what leadership needs to see and how to present it. 

 Identify risks, stalled decisions, and at-risk dependencies before they become problems.  

 Other duties as assigned. 

 
 About You 

 
 10+ years in leadership roles, with a proven track record in Program Management. 

 Exceptional ability to translate complex concepts into clear messages for diverse audiences. 

 Build and mentor a diverse and growing team of technical and non-technical Program Managers. 

 Strong data-driven decision-making skills to manage a complex portfolio of initiatives across a range of departments. 

 Operate with a high degree of autonomy defining the path for you and the team. 

 Deep understanding of how manufacturing and operations environments work — with 7+ years of experience driving programs in this space. 

 Comfort working in organizations without mature systems, clean data, or clear processes. 

 
 Bonus Points 

 
 Prior experience managing or developing a team of program managers. 

 Background in high-growth hardware, automation, or robotics environments. 

 Experience designing or overhauling operational processes at scale — service operations, order fulfillment, or manufacturing workflows. 

 
 
  

 Location 

 
 This is a hybrid position based out of our Salem office.

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $149,000 — $193,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

records.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
records.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies. 

 Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

 Purpose

 Guide the integration of cutting-edge manufacturing technologies into production, ensuring reliability, cost efficiency, and quality. This role shapes the future of Divergent’s manufacturing by enabling new processes, supporting high-mix hardware, and mentoring engineers to deliver industry-leading results.

 The Role

 
 Lead a multi-disciplinary team of manufacturing engineers responsible for driving design-for-manufacturing, process development, and implementation of advanced manufacturing methods across the DAPS manufacturing architecture.

 Oversee manufacturing requirements, process specifications, and root cause investigations to ensure reliable, high-quality production.

 Set team priorities, track projects, and mentor engineers to achieve critical company milestones.

 Develop industry-leading approaches to manufacturing process qualification, production scalability, and automation.

 Implement advanced manufacturing strategies in areas such as machining, additive manufacturing, assembly, bonding, coatings, and joining.

 Identify and deploy novel manufacturing technologies to improve quality, reduce cost, and increase throughput.

 Collaborate closely with design, materials, quality, and production teams to influence hardware design and production readiness.

 
  

 Basic Qualifications

 
 Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls 

 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related discipline.

 3+ years of experience in a leadership role within manufacturing engineering.

 8+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering role, with significant exposure to aerospace or defense industries.

 Proficiency in CAD software (e.g., Siemens NX, AutoCAD) and strong understanding of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T).

 Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems.

 Hands-on experience with advanced manufacturing techniques, including additive manufacturing, robotics, and automation.

 Proven track record of leading complex projects from concept through production, focusing on high-performance materials and high-reliability applications.

 
 Preferred Qualifications

 
 Master’s degree in a relevant engineering discipline.

 Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent expertise in continuous improvement methodologies.

 Familiarity with quality management systems like AS9100 or ISO 9001.

 Demonstrated ability to thrive in a high-tech, fast-paced startup environment with a passion for disrupting traditional manufacturing paradigms.

 
  

 Compensation

 
 Senior Manager / M07: $165,800 - $227,950

 
  

  
 Pay Range
 $142,900 — $227,950 USD 


 What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees: 

 
 Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

 Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

 Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

 Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.

 Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint. 

 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Divergent is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected characteristic. Divergent provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act. 
 EEO Poster  

 In order to adjust to changes in our business, it may become necessary to add, remove or modify certain duties and responsibilities, or to reassign you to another job position. From time to time you may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected.  
   
 E-Verify: Right to Work 
 Our company participates in E-Verify . E-Verify is a program that electronically confirms a candidate’s eligibility to work in the United States after completing the Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9). The information provided on the Form I-9 is compared to the records contained in the Social Security Administration and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) databases. This helps employers verify the identity and employment eligibility of newly hired employees. 
 Eligibility to Work Poster (English) |  Eligibility to Work Poster (Spanish) 
   
 Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO) 
 Pursuant to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance (FCIHO), we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 

 No agencies, no solicitations, and no calls please.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here. 
 

 
Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.  

 Overview :
Ursa is seeking a strong production leader who can lead and build a team to scale production with a focus on safety and best-in-class industrial engineering principles. Ursa has developed a novel manufacturing method that can surge production levels across various products, employing mixed model strategy and early design for manufacturability. This position will heavily influence the standardization and scaling of these production lines. We are seeking a leader who can transform this manufacturing method into high volume (25,000+ units per year in SMS and 500 units we year for HAVOC).

 Our operations team is involved with early conceptual designs through high-rate production of motors. This leader will demonstrate a track record of collaborating on scaled production and a desire to implement standards and change. The role will lead the manufacturing operations and industrial engineering teams, our build and mixing operations, logistics, and facilities. Demonstrated performance in this role will lead to operational ownership of additional product lines at the company beyond just solids. This is a high growth role .

 Success will be defined by the safe scaling of our products and how well we can exceed customer expectations on quality and cost. This leader must have a start-up mentality with the rigor of real production.

 Key Responsibilities :

 
 Lead and build the production team to scale manufacturing from conceptual design through high-rate production, focusing on safety, quality, and efficiency.

 Build high performing engineering teams, including industrial engineering and manufacturing engineering.

 Lead and grow shop floor teams. Drive cross training, efficient operations, and sustained growth.

 Set standards for capacity modeling, manufacturing scaling, and industrial engineering across Ursa Major

 Engage and influence ERP and MES deployment strategy in support of scalability.

 Implement and refine our novel manufacturing method to meet varying customer demand profiles while ensuring responsiveness and flexibility in production.

 Drive continuous improvement initiatives that ensure industry-leading safety and quality standards.

 Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate production requirements from the early design phase through to full-scale manufacturing.

 Collaborate the facilities and logistics to support both development activities and high-volume production, ensuring seamless operation of manufacturing =

 Foster a culture of operational excellence and innovation within the production teams.

 Define and track key performance metrics and daily production metrics to track production performance, cost control, and quality assurance, ensuring goals are met or exceeded.

 
 Qualifications :

 
 6+ years of experience in scaled production, preferably in aerospace, defense, or related industries.

 Proven track record in leading large-scale, high-volume manufacturing operations, with a focus on safety, quality, and cost-efficiency.

 Experience in manufacturing of energetics or other safety-critical products is highly desirable.

 Strong leadership and team-building skills, with the ability to motivate cross-functional teams in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

 Exceptional problem-solving and process optimization skills, with a track record of implementing innovative production methods.

 Ability to navigate complex supply chains and develop strong supplier partnerships.

 Experience working with government and defense customers

 Start-up mentality combined with the rigor and discipline needed for high-volume, real-world production.

 Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

 
  

 Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $180,000 - $220,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t  quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy. 

 Classification: Full-time Exempt

  
 
 
  

 Benefits Include: (Please note, Interns are not eligible for benefits) 

 
 Unlimited PTO - Vacation, Sick, Personal, and Bereavement

 Paid Parental and Adoptive Leave

 Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance

 Tax Advantage Accounts (HSA/FSA)

 Employer Paid Short and Long Term Disability, Basic Life, AD&D

 Additional Benefit Options Including Voluntary Life and Emergency Medical Transport

 EAP Program

 Retirement Savings Plan - 401k with Company Match

 
  

 How To Apply:  
Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by filling out the application below and clicking "Submit Application". This position will be posted for a minimum of 3 days and will remain open until filled or adjusted based on the volume of applicants. 

 

 NOTE: Research suggests that women and BIPOC individuals may self-select out of opportunities if they don't meet 100% of the job requirements. We encourage anyone who believes they have the skills and the drive necessary to succeed here to apply for this role.



  

 Must be a U.S. Person (this includes U.S. Citizens and Permanent Residents). 

  

 Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.  

  

 We’re an equal-opportunity employer. You will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status. 

  

 No outside recruiters, please.

records.title: VP of Business Systems and Operations

postedPay.title: VP of Business Systems and Operations

records.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats. 

 CHAOS Industries was founded in 2022 and has raised a total of $1 billion in funding from leading investors, including 8VC, Accel, and Valor Equity Partners. The company is headquartered in Los Angeles, with offices in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, San Diego, and London. For more information, please visit  www.chaosinc.com .

 Role Overview

 Build the applications and shared data platform behind the way CHAOS plans and runs the business. You’ll lead a service for Finance, People, and the rest of G&A, connecting core workflows to manufacturing, supply chain, and the commercial systems where the activity happens.

 Your mandate spans applications, integrations, data engineering, and rollout. You’ll own how the shared systems work together in production, with clear responsibilities for IT, Security, Internal Tools, and the teams that own shop-floor systems and data.

 Responsibilities

 
 Own the G&A systems portfolio, roadmap, vendors, and day-to-day service. Agree with business owners on what to build, buy, integrate, or retire.

 Build and run the shared data platform for planning, financial reporting, and operating analytics. Set standards for source ownership, data quality, traceability, and reconciliation.

 Lead integrations across ERP, HR, payroll, and manufacturing systems. Coordinate boundaries with shop-floor system owners and assign responsibility for production issues.

 Own planning tools with Finance. Connect actuals to budgets and forecasts and make the planning cycle usable for operators and functional leaders.

 Lead company-wide timekeeping and other tool rollouts from requirements and vendor selection through testing, launch, training, and adoption. Design project charging and approvals with People, Finance, and program teams.

 Support business systems and data integration for acquisitions. Build and lead a team spanning systems, integrations, and data engineering. Set expectations for releases, service reliability, documentation, and support.

 Partner with IT and Security on access and applicable defense-contractor controls. Report delivery progress, risks, and adoption outcomes to executive leadership.

 
 Minimum Requirements

 
 10+ years in business systems, data engineering, or business operations, including significant leadership responsibility.

 Built a production data platform and integrated ERP, HR, and manufacturing systems in a manufacturing or defense company.

 Led implementations across planning, finance systems, or timekeeping from business design through rollout and support.

 Built multidisciplinary teams and managed vendors or implementation partners. Can explain technical tradeoffs and decisions to executives, engineers, and business users.

 
 Preferred Requirements

 
 Experience using data quality and adoption measures to improve a shared platform after launch.

 Experience in defense, aerospace, or advanced manufacturing, including relevant government-contracting or security requirements.

 
 Why CHAOS? 

 
 Health Benefits: medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

 Additional benefits : 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

 Our Perks: rree daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

 Compensation Components: competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

 Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

 
 
 Salary Range: $300-$350k   



 The stated compensation range reflects only the targeted base compensation range and excludes additional earnings such as bonus, equity, and benefits. If your compensation requirements fall outside of the range, we still encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations.  

  

 
 Recruiting Agencies: CHAOS Industries does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach. Unsolicited submissions will not be reviewed or compensated.

 
  

 #LI-onsite

records.title: Director, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
records.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team:  

 The Reliability team at Relativity Space ensures quality is built into every stage of the Terran R design and production process, embedding reliability from the very beginning. The team works directly with design, manufacturing, test, and launch teams to stay close to the hardware, understand constraints, and proactively shape decisions. As the program moves from development into production and scaled operations, this is the time to establish the right processes, controls, and inspections without slowing progress. The team plays a key role in balancing risk, fostering a culture of ownership, and making sure speed never comes at the cost of reliability. Success means creating a quality system that scales with the Terran R program and Relativity as a whole. 

 About the Role: 

 
 Develop and lead a high-performing Supplier Development Engineering team, fostering ownership, technical rigor, and data-driven decision-making. 

 Set and execute the supplier development strategy, reliability roadmap, and SQMS processes to meet Terran R production, launch, and compliance requirements (AS9100/ISO 9001). 

 Drive supplier performance management, establishing key metrics and scorecards to improve PPM, yield, PPAP timing, and overall supplier capability. 

 Own major supplier risk escalation and resolution, guiding disciplined problem solving (e.g., 8D) and ensuring rapid recovery on quality or capacity issues. 

 Lead cross-functional alignment with Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain on supplier qualification, technical requirements, and NPI execution. 

 Oversee technical and operational execution, including supplier qualification, APQP/DFM/DFA, PPAP/FAIR approvals, and CI initiatives (Lean/Six Sigma) to ensure robust manufacturing and protect build schedules.   

 
 About You: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Industrial, or a related technical field) 

 10+ years of experience in Supplier Industrialization, Supplier Development, or Manufacturing Engineering, ideally within the aerospace or a high-reliability/safety-critical industry. 

 5+ years of direct people management experience, including coaching, mentorship, and performance management of an engineering team 

 Expert knowledge of quality systems (AS9100/ISO 9001) and core quality tools (APQP, PPAP, FAIRs, PFMEA, Control Plans), with a proven ability to influence the implementation and compliance of key quality initiatives. 

 Demonstrated capability to build processes from the ground up and successfully deploy them across diverse teams. 

 Willingness to travel up to 50% of the work week when needed.   

 
 Nice to haves but not required:    

 
 Master’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Industrial, or a related technical field). 

 Professional certification such as Six Sigma Black Belt, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or PMP. 

 Familiarity with high-volume inspection methods and data-driven acceptance methods. 

 Strong knowledge of enterprise applications (i.e., PLM, ERP, MES) and proficient in data analysis.   

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $195,000 — $293,000 USD 


 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

records.title: Director, Accounting – Manufacturing
records.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role
Crusoe is looking for a Director of Accounting to own accounting, cost accounting and financial reporting for its manufacturing business. You'll report to the Corporate Controller and lead a multi-site team of 8+ and act as the accounting partner to Manufacturing leadership. You'll also build the cost, inventory and control infrastructure the business needs as production grows to meet demand for Crusoe's AI infrastructure.



Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy

 - Lead, build and develop a team of 8+ across multiple manufacturing facilities. Set the team's structure, hiring plan and development path as the business grows.

 - Act as the primary finance partner to manufacturing leadership (operations, supply chain, engineering, quality and procurement). Turn plant and assembly metrics into financial insight and decisions.

 - Drive financial accountability across operations by setting cost targets, tracking performance and influencing decisions on capacity, make-vs-buy, sourcing and pricing.

 - Advise executive leadership on product and program margins, cost-reduction opportunities and the financial impact of design, material and process changes.

Cost Accounting & Inventory

 - Own the cost accounting framework, including standard cost methodology, the annual standard-setting process, overhead absorption and labor rates.

 - Set and oversee inventory accounting policy, including valuation, WIP, high-value long-lead components, reserves and excess/obsolete inventory. Own the cycle count and physical inventory programs across all sites.

 - Lead analysis of manufacturing variances (purchase price, usage, labor, overhead), yield and productivity. Turn the results into actionable cost-improvement initiatives.

 - Own new-product and new-program cost estimates and margin modeling in partnership with Engineering and Sales.

Close, Reporting & Controls

 - Be accountable for a timely, accurate month-end close for the manufacturing entity. Present results, key drivers and risks to the Controller, CAO and operations leadership.

 - Ensure US GAAP compliance and own the manufacturing control environment, building it out to a SOX-ready, audit-ready standard. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors on manufacturing and inventory matters.

 - Lead the manufacturing entity's annual budget and rolling forecasts, working with FP&A.

Systems & Scale

 - Act as the accounting owner for the ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, work orders, costing) and lead system improvements and implementations.

 - Design, document and continuously improve scalable processes, with a focus on automation, as new facilities and product lines come online.



Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting. CPA or CMA required.

 - 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 5+ years in manufacturing or cost accounting and 3+ years leading teams (including managers).

 - Proven ownership of standard costing, inventory valuation and variance analysis in a complex, multi-site manufacturing environment.

 - Deep experience with ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, job and work-order costing). ERP implementation experience is a plus.

 - Experience with complex inventory, such as WIP, engineered-to-order or high-value long-lead components.

 - Strong knowledge of US GAAP and internal controls. SOX, public-company or Big 4 experience is a plus.

 - Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills.

 - High operational credibility: comfortable on the factory floor and able to influence senior operations and engineering leaders.

 - Track record of scaling teams, processes and systems in a high-growth environment.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 - $200,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

records.title: Director, Ops Analysis (R5036)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is building intelligent autonomy systems for the defense of service members and civilians. The Hivemind Solutions organization applies Shield AI’s autonomy stack to mission-critical systems across air, maritime, strike, weapons, space, and collaborative autonomy domains.

We are seeking a Director, Operations Analysis to lead a team responsible for turning operational problems into quantitative insights that shape product strategy, engineering priorities, customer engagement, and mission outcomes. This leader will manage and grow a high-performing Operations Analysis team that uses modeling, simulation, wargaming, campaign analysis, and mission-level trade studies to help determine what Hivemind should build, why it matters, and how it performs in realistic operational contexts.

This is a leadership role for someone who can operate at the intersection of autonomy, military operations, mission engineering, modeling and simulation, product strategy, and customer-facing analysis. The right candidate will be technically credible, analytically rigorous, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to translate complex operational questions into clear recommendations for executives, engineers, business development leaders, and government customers.

What you'll do:

 - 

 - Lead and manage the Hivemind Solutions Operations Analysis team, including hiring, mentoring, prioritization, performance management, and technical direction.

 - Build an operations analysis capability that directly informs Hivemind product strategy, autonomy roadmap decisions, customer pursuits, and program execution.

 - Define and execute mission analysis, campaign analysis, force-on-force studies, CONOPS evaluations, and operational trade studies across multiple Hivemind product domains.

 - Partner with Product, Architecture, Systems Engineering, Business Development, Strategy, and Program teams to translate operational problems into analytical studies and actionable product recommendations.

 - Develop analysis plans that connect mission objectives, operational assumptions, threat environments, system performance, autonomy behaviors, and measurable mission outcomes.

 - Guide the use of tools such as AFSIM, NGTS, STK, MATLAB, Python, custom simulations, and other modeling environments to evaluate mission effectiveness and operational value.

 - Establish standards for analytical rigor, model credibility, assumption tracking, sensitivity analysis, uncertainty characterization, and communication of results.

 - Create clear, executive-ready briefings that explain what was analyzed, what assumptions were made, what the results mean, and what decisions should follow.

 - Support customer engagements by developing compelling, technically grounded analysis that demonstrates the operational value of Hivemind-enabled systems.

 - Work with engineering teams to identify the autonomy behaviors, system capabilities, interfaces, performance parameters, and test data needed to improve model fidelity.

 - Help shape product requirements by connecting operational outcomes to measurable system and autonomy performance needs.

 - Build reusable analysis frameworks, scenarios, vignettes, and metrics that can scale across programs and domains.

 - Represent the Operations Analysis function in internal technical reviews, roadmap discussions, capture strategy sessions, and customer-facing meetings.

 - 

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations research, applied mathematics, computer science, physics, aerospace, systems engineering, data science, or a related technical field.

 - 5+ years of experience leading teams, projects, or technical analysis efforts.

 - Experience using modeling and simulation to inform real product, system, program, or operational decisions.

 - Strong understanding of military operations, mission planning, force employment, kill chains, sensing, communications, autonomy, aircraft systems, weapons systems, or related defense concepts.

 - Ability to translate ambiguous operational questions into structured analysis plans, quantitative methods, and decision-quality outputs.

 - Experience working with engineering, product, business development, strategy, or customer-facing teams.

 - Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders and customers with clarity, confidence, and analytical discipline.

 - Ability to work in a fast-paced environment where priorities evolve quickly and analysis must support real business and technical decisions.

 - U.S. citizenship and eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred qualifications:

 - 

 - Master’s degree or PhD in operations research, engineering, applied mathematics, data science, aerospace, systems engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Experience with AFSIM, NGTS, STK, MATLAB, Python, Cameo, custom simulation environments, or other mission and campaign analysis tools.

 - Experience analyzing autonomous systems, collaborative autonomy, uncrewed aircraft, crewed-uncrewed teaming, electronic warfare, space systems, missile systems, maritime systems, or air combat operations.

 - Experience supporting defense product development, advanced concepts, government capture efforts, experimentation, test planning, or mission engineering.

 - Familiarity with model validation, verification, credibility assessment, sensitivity analysis, design of experiments, and uncertainty quantification.

 - Experience building analysis teams, establishing technical standards, and scaling analytical capabilities across multiple stakeholders or product lines.

 - Prior military, government laboratory, FFRDC/UARC, defense contractor, or aerospace experience.

 - Active U.S. security clearance.

 - In this role, success means the Operations Analysis team becomes a trusted decision engine for Hivemind Solutions. The team’s work should not sit on a shelf. It should shape what we build, how we prioritize, how we explain operational value to customers, and how we make hard trade decisions across product lines.
 
 A successful manager will build a team that is technically rigorous, operationally grounded, fast-moving, and deeply connected to the business. They will ensure that analysis is not treated as an after-the-fact briefing function, but as a core part of product development, strategy, and customer engagement.

Why this role matters:

 - Autonomy changes what is operationally possible, but only if we understand where it creates real mission advantage. The Operations Analysis team helps answer that question. This team connects Hivemind’s technical capabilities to measurable operational outcomes, helping Shield AI make better product decisions and helping customers understand the mission impact of intelligent autonomous systems.
 
 If you want to lead a team that sits at the center of autonomy, strategy, engineering, and operational decision-making, this role is for you.

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a highly driven Sr. Manager Materials Planning & Logistics to lead supply planning, material readiness, production planning, and logistics execution for next-generation autonomous aircraft development programs and a new greenfield manufacturing facility. This leadership role is accountable for establishing the people, processes, systems, and infrastructure required to support rapid product development, new product introduction, and the transition to scalable rate production. 

The ideal candidate combines strong operational leadership with hands-on execution, thrives in fast-paced environments, and has experience building manufacturing and supply chain capabilities from the ground up. You will work cross-functionally with Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Operations teams.  

What you'll do:

Development Program Materials Planning  

 - Own the materials planning, production control, inventory, warehousing, and logistics strategy. 

 - Partner with Engineering, Program Management, and Procurement to develop and maintain accurate build plans that are aligned with program milestones.   

 - Define and monitor key performance indicators for schedule attainment, material availability, shortage reduction, inventory health, work-order execution, and planning accuracy. 

 - Identify long-lead material risks and implement mitigation strategies to protect schedule. 

 - Oversee the development and execution of material recovery plans. 

 - Drive engineering change management processes to support rapid development and ECO implementation.   

 - Develop planning models that support rapid prototyping, design iteration, and low-rate initial production activities.   

 - Support executive-level program and operations reviews by clearly communicating material status, risks, business impacts, and required decisions. 

Greenfield Facility Build & Operational Readiness  

 - Lead planning and logistics readiness activities for a new manufacturing facility.   

 - Design and implement warehouse, stockroom, and material flow processes from receiving through point-of-use consumption.   

 - Establish inventory control procedures, material storage standards, and transaction discipline.   

 - Partner with Manufacturing Engineering and Facilities teams to optimize material movement and operational efficiency.   

Team Leadership  

 - Create a culture focused on accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and mission execution.   

 - Establish standard work and training programs.   

 - Drive cross-functional collaboration to solve complex challenges.   

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field.   

 - 7+ years of experience in materials planning, inventory management, or supply chain operations.   

 - Experience supporting complex hardware development programs in aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environments.   

 - Demonstrated experience implementing or scaling material planning and inventory management processes.   

 - Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems and supply chain planning methodologies.   

 - Experience managing material readiness for new product introduction (NPI) and engineering development programs.   

 - Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment with evolving priorities.   

 - Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills.   

 - U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain/maintain a security clearance 

Preferred qualifications:

 - Experience supporting greenfield manufacturing facility launches or major facility expansions.   

 - Aerospace, defense, unmanned systems, or advanced technology manufacturing experience.   

 - Experience with Oracle, SAP, Costpoint, or similar ERP platforms.   

 - APICS/ASCM certifications (CPIM, CSCP) or equivalent.   

 - Familiarity with ITAR, EAR, DFARS, and government contracting requirements.   

 - Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or operational excellence experience.   

 - Experience supporting production ramp and transition from development to rate manufacturing.   

Why Shield AI:

At Shield AI, you'll help build technology that matters. You'll work alongside world-class engineers, operators, and innovators solving some of the most challenging problems in autonomy and national security. This is a unique opportunity to shape the foundation of a rapidly growing aerospace and defense company while helping bring revolutionary autonomous systems into operational service.

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


ABOUT SHIELD AI:

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense technology company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We’re looking for a hands-on quality leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 

You will build the aircraft quality organization and establish the quality capability for our new Seattle-area production facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll own product and process quality across prototype, pre-series and production builds, ensuring that lessons from development become effective controls as the program scales. 

This role owns the Quality Management System, quality engineering, inspection, nonconformance management and audit readiness for the X-BAT manufacturing operation. You’ll partner with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Production and Supply Chain to prevent defects, resolve recurring problems and deliver aircraft that meet technical, customer and applicable regulatory requirements. 

We need a technically credible leader who can build practical, scalable systems, make sound decisions under schedule pressure and challenge senior stakeholders constructively while keeping execution moving. 

What you'll do:

 - Build quality into prototype and launch 
 
 - Lead quality planning and execution for X-BAT prototype and development builds, establishing appropriate inspection, test evidence and build records as designs evolve.

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a Strategy & Operations Director to help define enterprise strategy and ensure its operational execution. This role offers immersive exposure to the company’s most critical decisions — spanning aircraft systems, AI software (Hivemind), autonomy hardware, and international growth.

As a core member of the Strategy & Operations team, you’ll apply structured problem‑solving, financial rigor, and operational discipline to turn strategic priorities into actionable, measurable outcomes. The role combines high‑performance expectations with a strong learning and development environment — ideal for professionals seeking to grow into future strategy, operations, or general management leaders.

What you'll do:

 - Enterprise Strategy Development:
 
 - Lead the multi‑year strategic planning and annual operating strategy cycles.
 
 - Evaluate portfolio tradeoffs across platforms, software, hardware, and emerging growth vectors.
 
 - Conduct market sizing, competitive analysis, and scenario modeling across U.S. and allied defense markets.
 
 Capital Allocation & Business Case Rigor:
 
 - Build financial models and analytic frameworks for investment decisions (new platforms, manufacturing, international expansion).
 
 - Assess TAM, margin structure, capital intensity, payback, and risk‑adjusted returns.
 
 - Contribute to the development of enterprise‑wide capital allocation frameworks and governance processes.
 
 Operationalization of Strategy:
 
 - Translate strategic priorities into cross‑functional execution plans with defined KPIs and milestones.
 
 - Track and report on progress through structured operating cadences (monthly and quarterly performance reviews).
 
 - Identify bottlenecks, analyze root causes, and recommend actionable solutions to sustain execution velocity.

Required qualifications:

 - Min 12+ years of experience with Bachelors, 8+ with Masters, and 5+ with PhD.

 - Min 4+ years’ experience in a top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy or other high‑rigor roles.

 - Strong analytical and conceptual problem‑solving abilities.

 - Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive insight through analysis.

 - Financial modeling and analytical capability (unit economics, forecasting, scenario analysis).

 - Experience or strong interest in complex, technical, or regulated industries (aerospace, defense, AI, or advanced manufacturing preferred).

 - Ability to work collaboratively across teams and influence senior stakeholders.

 - U.S. citizenship required (ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance).

records.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with  neffy® , the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture. 



 

 THE OPPORTUNITY 

 
 The Director / Senior Director, Technical Operations will provide strategic leadership for ARS' external manufacturing and Technical Operations activities supporting the continued development, lifecycle management, and commercial supply of neffy™. The successful candidate will combine strong technical, business, and operational leadership with cross-functional influence and CMO management expertise to drive manufacturing excellence, scalable operations, and reliable product supply.

 This role is accountable for manufacturing strategy, CMO performance, process and technology lifecycle management, resolution of major technical issues, and execution of key Technical Operations initiatives across the ARS outsourced manufacturing network. Working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners, the position leads complex cross-functional programs, oversees partner performance and agreements, manages departmental planning and budgets, and ensures technical, supply, regulatory, and business risks are appropriately identified, assessed, and escalated.



   ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Provide leadership for Technical Operations programs and external manufacturing activities, establishing strategy, priorities, scope, timelines, deliverables, responsibilities, budgets, risks, and key decision points.

 Own senior-level Technical Operations relationships with key CMOs/CDMOs and other external partners; establish governance, performance expectations, escalation pathways, and accountability for delivery against manufacturing and business commitments.

 Provide technical leadership for formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process characterization, process validation/PPQ, continued process verification, and manufacturing lifecycle management, as applicable.

 Oversee clinical and commercial manufacturing strategy and execution in coordination with external manufacturers and internal stakeholders; ensure appropriate Technical Operations support for critical manufacturing campaigns, product launches, and supply requirements.

 Provide senior technical review and oversight of manufacturing and process documentation, process performance, significant vendor changes, investigations, annual/product reviews, and significant deviations, out-of-specification or atypical results, and complex manufacturing problems; ensure robust technical investigation, root-cause analysis, effective corrective and preventive actions, continued process control, and reliable manufacturing in partnership with Quality Assurance.

 Lead technical assessments of significant manufacturing, process, component, and supplier changes and coordinate evaluation of quality, regulatory, supply, financial, and business impacts with appropriate functional stakeholders.

 Establish and review manufacturing, supply, and external partner performance metrics and KPIs, including service, quality, on-time delivery, right-first-time, cost, capacity, and other appropriate measures; drive lifecycle improvements, operational excellence, capacity planning, cost improvement, and risk-reduction initiatives across the external network.

 Lead external partner business and technical governance, including selection and strategic development of CMOs, CDMOs, suppliers, and other critical partners; establish performance expectations and governance mechanisms, oversee business reviews, scopes of work, proposals, change orders, contract and supply agreement support, and escalation of commercial or operational issues; and develop business continuity, capacity, and second-source strategies for critical manufacturing capabilities and materials.

 Represent Technical Operations on cross-functional program and leadership teams; communicate manufacturing strategy, program status, significant risks, financial implications, and recommendations to senior management and key stakeholders.

 Partner with Regulatory Affairs on CMC strategy, regulatory submissions, post-approval changes, and health authority responses; ensure manufacturing plans and technical decisions are aligned with regulatory commitments.

 Lead Technical Operations business planning and continuous improvement initiatives, including departmental budget development with Finance/FP&A, contract lifecycle management, operational process standardization, and long-range manufacturing planning.

 Provide leadership and governance for commercial supply operations managed within Technical Operations, including 3PL and distribution partner performance, inventory and supply continuity, shipping/returns interfaces, and support of product launches and new markets.

 Oversee the commercial serialization program, including serialized packaging operations, EPCIS data exchange with trading partners and service providers, and compliance with applicable Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements; ensure issues are appropriately escalated and resolved cross-functionally.

 Provide leadership and oversight for clinical supply operations, including clinical material planning, packaging, labeling, distribution, inventory/expiry management, and coordination of Interactive Response Technology/Interactive Web Response System (IRT/IWRS) activities with Clinical Operations and external vendors.

 
   KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: 

 
 Broad and deep knowledge of cGMP, pharmaceutical manufacturing, quality systems, formulation and process development, scale-up, technology transfer, process validation, lifecycle management, and applicable CMC regulatory expectations, with the technical credibility to critically challenge external partner data, conclusions, and recommendations.

 Demonstrated leadership of outsourced manufacturing relationships, complex cross-functional programs, and teams, including governance, performance management, contract/scope management, budgeting, executive-level escalation, influence without direct authority, and accountability of external partners for performance and commitments.

 Strong strategic, analytical, and problem-solving capability, with demonstrated ability to evaluate complex technical and business issues, balance risk, cost, supply continuity, and regulatory considerations, and make sound recommendations.

 Excellent written, verbal, negotiation, and presentation skills with the ability to influence across functions and organizational levels and communicate effectively with senior management and external partners.

 Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to translate budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, contract terms, and operational metrics into business decisions and actions.

 Experience establishing scalable Technical Operations processes and systems; proficiency with Microsoft Office and relevant project, reporting, or data-management tools.

 Demonstrated knowledge of commercial and clinical supply operations within an outsourced model, including 3PL management, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and clinical supply/IRT/IWRS processes.

 Must be able to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 25% to support external manufacturing partners, governance meetings, and key manufacturing activities.

 
   EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry, chemical engineering, engineering, or related scientific/technical discipline; an advanced degree (MS, PhD, or MBA) is preferred. An acceptable combination of education and relevant experience will also be considered.

 Minimum of 10+ years of relevant pharmaceutical/biotechnology experience in Technical Operations, manufacturing, process development, CMC, or related functions, with demonstrated leadership of complex programs and external manufacturing relationships.

 Significant experience managing external CMOs/CDMOs in an outsourced operating model and supporting GMP clinical and commercial manufacturing is required.

 Experience with drug-device combination products, nasal/inhalation products, sterile manufacturing, process validation/PPQ, commercial product launch, and lifecycle management is strongly preferred.

 Experience supporting CMC regulatory strategy and submissions, major investigations and change controls, vendor/supply agreements, budget planning, and business continuity is preferred. Prior people-management or functional leadership experience is strongly preferred.

 Experience overseeing commercial distribution and 3PL partners, serialization/EPCIS and DSCSA compliance, and clinical supply operations including IRT/IWRS is strongly preferred; experience across multiple of these areas is preferred.

 
 
 At ARS, we are proud to offer a highly competitive compensation & benefits package.  

  



 
 The full-time salary range for this posted position is $225,000 to $275,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law. 



  
 This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here:  ARS Careers Page 

 ARS Pharmaceuticals believes in Equal Opportunity for all and is committed to ensuring all individuals, including individuals with disabilities, have an opportunity to apply for those positions that they are interested in and qualify for without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, citizenship, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic. ARS Pharmaceuticals is also committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals so that an individual can perform their job-related duties. If you are interested in applying for an employment opportunity and require special assistance or an accommodation to apply due to a disability, please contact us at careers@ars-pharma.com 

 The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected for the requisition or the requisition has a sufficient number of applications.

records.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good. 

 At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

 Your Impact 

 You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.

 As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.

 Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.

 What You’ll Do 

 Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
 Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
 Direct Reports:   Individual Contributors

 Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers

 
 Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments

 Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments

 Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact

 Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership

 Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability

 Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders

 
 Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes

 
 Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution

 Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed

 Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption

 Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design

 Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable

 
 Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio

 
 Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs

 Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment

 Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse

 Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership

 Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook

 
 Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery

 
 Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning

 Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified

 Establish expectations for validation, observability, fallback paths, maintainability, documentation, and responsible use of sensitive data

 Ensure solutions uphold CJIS requirements, evidence integrity, privacy, approved-tooling standards, and other applicable security controls

 Encourage practical use of AI to accelerate work while preserving human ownership of architecture, accuracy, and outcomes

 
 Turn Field Learning Into Organizational Leverage

 
 Build mechanisms for Mission Engineers to document and share reusable workflows, integrations, frameworks, and playbooks

 Identify patterns across agencies and help convert successful one-off solutions into repeatable capabilities

 Create strong feedback loops with Product and Engineering around recurring workflow friction, unmet operational needs, and product opportunities

 Partner with Mission Operators, Customer Success, Deployment, Professional Services, Support, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Enablement so agencies experience coordinated execution

 Share portfolio insights with senior leaders to influence investment, prioritization, staffing, and the evolution of the Mission Engineering operating model

 
 Lead Executive and Agency Engagement

 
 Build trusted relationships with command staff, agency executives, technical leaders, and internal senior leadership

 Serve as a senior partner during agency-impacting incidents, high-visibility deployments, and moments that require clear trade-offs or executive alignment

 Translate complex technical and operational issues into decisions that are clear to both technical teams and executive audiences

 Coach Mission Engineers to challenge requests constructively, communicate candidly, and leave stakeholders with a practical path forward

 
 What You Bring

 Required

 
 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical delivery, systems integration, solutions engineering, implementation consulting, operational transformation, or comparable environments

 5+ years leading and developing senior technical individual contributors in customer-facing organizations

 Demonstrated success coaching teams that deliver secure, production-ready solutions in complex customer environments

 Experience leading distributed or field-based teams across multiple customers, regions, or engagement models

 A record of improving technical execution, adoption, operational outcomes, and delivery consistency across a portfolio

 Broad technical fluency across SaaS platforms, cloud services, APIs, networking, hardware, integrations, data workflows, and AI-enabled technologies

 Executive presence with the ability to earn trust, communicate trade-offs, and guide decisions with command staff and senior leaders

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to distinguish isolated issues from patterns that require a scalable solution

 A data-informed leadership approach using baselines, production delivery, adoption, operational improvement, quality, and reuse to evaluate performance

 Comfort leading through ambiguity while creating clarity around ownership, priorities, and success criteria

 Ability to obtain and maintain CJIS compliance and exercise sound judgment with highly sensitive information

 
 Preferred

 
 Experience in public safety, law enforcement, defense, government technology, or another mission-critical operating environment

 Familiarity with CAD, RMS, digital evidence, real-time operations, or integrated public safety ecosystems

 Experience leading teams that build automations, integrations, operational workflows, internal tools, or AI-enabled solutions

 Experience converting field-developed solutions into reusable frameworks, product improvements, or organizational playbooks

 Familiarity with technical talent development, competency frameworks, or academy-style enablement programs

 
 Additional Information

 We recognize that leaders may arrive through different paths. If you have developed technically curious customer-facing teams, helped people turn ambiguous operational problems into working solutions, and care deeply about measurable customer impact, we encourage you to apply.

 Benefits that Benefit You

 
 Competitive salary and 401k with employer match

 Discretionary paid time off

 Paid parental leave for all

 Medical, Dental, Vision plans

 Fitness Programs

 Emotional & Mental Wellness support

 Learning & Development programs

 And yes, we have snacks in our offices

 
  

 Benefits listed herein may vary depending on the nature of your employment and the location where you work.
 Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Important Notes 

 The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions. 

 Some roles may also require legal eligibility to work in a firearms environment. 

 We collect personal information from applicants to evaluate candidates for employment. You may request access, deletion, or exercise other CCPA rights at  axongreenhousesupport@axon.com  or via our  Axon Privacy Web Form . For more information, please see the Your California Privacy Rights section of our  Applicant and Candidate Privacy Notice. 

 Axon’s mission is to Protect Life and is committed to the well-being and safety of its employees as well as Axon’s impact on the environment. All Axon employees must be aware of and committed to the appropriate environmental, health, and safety regulations, policies, and procedures. Axon employees are empowered to report safety concerns as they arise and activities potentially impacting the environment. 

 We are an equal opportunity employer that promotes justice, advances equity, values diversity and fosters inclusion. We’re committed to hiring the best talent — regardless of race, creed, color, ancestry, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances — and empowering all of our employees so they can do their best work. If you have a disability or special need that requires assistance or accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email recruitingops@axon.com.  Please note that this email address is for accommodation purposes only. Axon will not respond to inquiries for other purposes. 

 Phishing alert:  Axon will never ask you to pay for any part of the hiring process, including training, equipment, or background checks.
