records.title: Staff Quality Engineer
records.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




POSITION OVERVIEW

The Staff Quality Engineer serves as the VP of Quality's senior technical quality expert responsible for driving multi-site RCCA culture, supporting engineering and manufacturing quality. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, this role leads enterprise-wide technical investigations, drives engineering-based Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), and partners across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Product, and Mission Operations to improve product reliability and operational performance.

This position applies deep engineering expertise to identify fundamental technical failure mechanisms, validate corrective actions through engineering analysis and testing, and eliminate systemic product and process risks.

The Staff Quality Engineer operates across multiple manufacturing sites and product lines, working with cross functional teams on design opportunities, manufacturing processes, and operational readiness while establishing best practices for technical problem solving across the enterprise.




TECHNICAL PROBLEM SOLVING

 - Apply structured engineering methodologies to determine true physical, process, software, or systems root causes—not simply procedural gaps.

 - Utilize advanced analytical tools including Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone, 5 Why, Statistical Analysis, Tolerance Stack Analysis, and FMEA.

 - Validate corrective actions using engineering data, experimentation, testing, and verification.

 - Drive permanent corrective actions that eliminate recurrence across products and manufacturing sites.




MULTI-SITE QUALITY LEADERSHIP

 - Provide technical quality leadership across multiple manufacturing locations.

 - Standardize RCCA methodologies and engineering investigations across the enterprise.

 - Coach site Quality Engineers on advanced engineering problem solving.

 - Lead enterprise technical reviews for recurring issues and customer escapes.

 - Support rapid problem escalation and recovery during production interruptions.




ROOT CAUSE & CORRECTIVE ACTION (RCCA)

 - Lead enterprise RCCA for manufacturing defects, supplier escapes, customer returns, field failures, and reliability issues.

 - Ensure investigations identify technical root causes rather than symptoms.




MANUFACTURING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

 - Improve manufacturing capability through engineering analysis.

 - Reduce defects through process optimization rather than increased inspection.

 - Support New Product Introduction (NPI) Quality activities across multiple product lines.




CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, Product Management, Mission Operations, and Executive Leadership.

 - Present technical findings and recommendations to cross functional teams.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering.

 - 10+ years of engineering aerospace, defense, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 - Demonstrated success solving complex engineering problems.

 - Extensive experience leading engineering-based RCCA.

 - Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations.

 - Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

 - Must be able to travel 30-50% of the time.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Design and development engineering management experience




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Establish an enterprise technical RCCA methodology across all manufacturing sites.

 - Reduce quality escapes through permanent corrective actions.

 - Improve manufacturing FPY.

 - Mentor Quality Engineers in advanced engineering problem solving.




BENEFITS

 - Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

 - Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

 - Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

 - Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

 - Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

 - Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

 - Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

 - Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

 - Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

 - Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

records.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight. This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




BUILDING ON A HEAD START

Skydio is the largest U.S.-based drone manufacturer, and we have treated secure supply chains as a strategic investment from the start. All of our current drone solutions, including X10, Dock for X10 and R10, are on the Blue UAS Cleared List. We have outgrown four U.S. manufacturing facilities in eight years. In April 2026 we committed $3.5 billion over five years to expand U.S. manufacturing through our SkyForge initiative, R&D and supply chain development. That includes a new U.S. factory five times the size of our current space and directing more than $1 billion to domestic suppliers. Through SkyForge, select suppliers will co-locate production with Skydio and work alongside our engineers, expanding and in some cases starting domestic manufacturing of critical parts. You will spearhead the SkyForge initiative and help decide where that investment goes and make sure it pays off: which components to onshore first, which suppliers to develop, and which capabilities to bring in-house.

Skydio is committed to becoming a world class manufacturing company. U.S. policy is moving toward secure, domestic drone supply chains and evolving policy on component origin, supplier eligibility, market access and import duties are raising the bar for every manufacturer in the industry. Skydio has historically been at the forefront of investing in US manufacturing and blue supply, and we are doubling down on our commitments to ensure America leads the next frontier of flight . This role will drive the strategic plan to build the drone manufacturing mecca and the stable and compliant supply chains that feed it.




WHAT YOU'LL NAVIGATE

 - NDAA restrictions and the American Security Drone Act

 - The Blue UAS Cleared List and Blue UAS Framework

 - The DDP Supply Chain Framework and its phased component requirements

 - The FCC Covered List and equipment authorization

 - Section 232 tariffs and country-of-origin requirements




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Regulatory Partner: You will work closely with our regulatory team to understand current regulations, policy direction and will work directly with key partners setting this policy to help influence

 - Supply Chain and Manufacturing Strategy: Determine which capabilities and technologies we onshore, vertically integrate or partner on to build robust and compliant supply chains

 - Onshoring and supplier development: Set priorities for securing and onshoring supply across our critical commodities with the commodity teams. Where a domestic or allied supply base does not yet exist, decide whether to develop a supplier (including through SkyForge), bring the work in-house, or design around the constraint.

 - Make-versus-buy and vertical integration: Assess which production we should bring into our U.S. facilities and build the case with Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Finance. A well-supported recommendation against integration is as valuable as one for it.

 - Product compliance risk: Maintain a live, evidence-backed view of where each product line stands against each regulation. Translate it into schedule, revenue and cost terms the leadership team can act on, and report on a regular cadence.

 - Supplier-of-record decisions during design: Work alongside Global Supply Managers (GSMs) and hardware engineering during NPI to set SPOR. Bring the regulatory screen into design reviews early enough that engineering can still act on it.

 - Multi-tier traceability: Stand up bill-of-materials traceability to tier three and beyond, with country of origin and chain of custody, across purchased and in-house components.

 - Compliance and cost together: Find moves that serve compliance, tariff and domestic-content goals at once, and look for other opportunities to drive domestic sourcing to cost parity with traditional supply chains.
 
 


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

90 days: A complete risk baseline across products and regulations, separating hard blockers from cost problems, with named owners for every gap and a first readout to leadership.

3 months: An approved sourcing and supplier-development plan, a first vertical integration recommendation, and compliance screening built into design reviews. Each product line has a decided market-access pathway.

6 months: No launch is surprised by a compliance gap. Onshoring and supplier investments are prioritized by where they build the most durable advantage, and make-versus-buy decisions weigh compliance, tariff and domestic-content effects together.



WHAT YOU BRING


REQUIRED

 - 10+ years in supply chain, manufacturing operations, commodity management or operations strategy, including at least 3 in a regulated hardware environment where sourcing decisions carried legal or contractual consequences.

 - Experience influencing component and supplier selection during design, through NPI, design reviews, or SPOR and approved vendor list (AVL) decisions.

 - Credibility with both a sourcing organization and a factory. You can discuss capacity, tooling and yield as fluently as supplier qualification.

 - Accountable ownership of a multi-tier country-of-origin, supplier compliance or trade compliance program.

 - A make-versus-buy or vertical integration analysis you personally built and defended, including capex and ramp assumptions.

 - A track record of turning technical findings into executive decisions, and of changing engineering or sourcing decisions you had no formal authority over.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.


PREFERRED

 - Working knowledge of NDAA §889/§848, country-of-origin and substantial-transformation analysis, Buy American domestic-content tests, or DFARS and FAR flow-downs

 - Background in in-house manufacturing, UAS, aerospace and defense, defense electronics, or EMS and contract manufacturing

 - Commodity experience in batteries and cells, motors and magnetics, imaging or thermal sensors, or PCB and PCBA

 - Experience standing up a production line or bringing an outsourced process in-house

 - Experience with a Blue UAS or Green UAS submission, or a DCMA or DCSA assessment

 - Experience developing domestic or allied-country suppliers from scratch




HOW THE ROLE FITS

 - Reports to: Head of Hardware Operations. Individual contributor at hire, with a path to building a small team as the program grows.

 - Peers: VP of Supply Chain and VP of Manufacturing.

 - Partners: Regulatory, Manufacturing Engineering, GSMs, Program Leads, Trade Compliance and Finance.

 - Visibility: Regular briefings to the leadership team on SkyForge progress. Several decisions this role informs are capital-allocation decisions.

Compensation: At Skydio, our compensation packages for regular, full-time employees include competitive base salaries, equity in the form of stock options, and comprehensive benefits packages. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. Relocation assistance may also be provided for eligible roles. The annual base salary range for this position is $229,500 - $302,500*. Fundamentally, we believe that equity is the key to long-term financial growth, and we ensure all regular, full-time employees have the opportunity to significantly benefit from the company's success. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to enroll in the Company’s group health insurance plans. Regular, full-time employees are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. This position and all associated benefits are subject to applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as the Company’s policies and eligibility criteria.

*Compensation for certain positions may vary based on the position’s location.

#LI-AR2 

At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws.

For positions located in the United States of America, Skydio, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit https://www.e-verify.gov/

records.title: Director, Product Quality
records.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 We are looking for a hands-on, high-impact Director, Product Quality  to lead our Field Quality and Failure Analysis engineering teams. In this role, you will hold ultimate accountability for overall field quality, reliability performance, and fleet health across all deployed commercial products. 

 You are a seasoned practitioner of rigorous problem-solving methodologies (8D, 5-Why, DMAIC) with a proven track record of diving deep into complex electromechanical, hardware, and firmware failures. You will bridge the gap between field service operations, customer sites, supplier quality, and internal product design teams to ensure field issues are contained rapidly, root-caused definitively, and prevented permanently. 

 About the Work 

 
 Own Field Quality & Fleet Health: Establish, monitor, and report on key field quality metrics (e.g., MTBI, MTTF, ARR, issue escape rates, service ticket turnaround time) for all shipping products and customer deployments. 

 Lead Failure Analysis (FA) & CAPA: Lead and grow a dedicated team of Failure Analysis Engineers. Drive rigorous Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes for field returns, hardware bugs, and system-level failures. 

 Field Containment & Rapid Response: Establish immediate containment protocols for critical field escalations, safety events, and unexpected fleet-wide failure trends to minimize customer downtime. 

 Cross-Functional Feedback Loop: Serve as the critical bridge between Field Operations, Customer Success, Hardware Engineering, Software/Firmware, and Supplier Quality. Drive design-for-reliability (DFR) feedback directly into next-generation product engineering. 

 Manage Closed-Loop Quality Systems: Implement and maintain robust Closed-Loop Corrective Action (CAPA) tracking across multi-site field deployments and repair depots. 

 Executive Communication & Governance: Host regular Field Quality Reviews with leadership, presenting objective data, failure Pareto analyses, root-cause findings, and measurable CAPA progress. 

 
 About You 

 
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. 

 Experience: 10+ years of experience in Quality Engineering, Field Quality, or Reliability Engineering within high-complexity hardware industries (Robotics, Automotive/EV, Aerospace, Autonomous Systems, or Complex Industrial Equipment). 

 Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading technical engineering teams (FA, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering). 

 Hands-on Expertise: Deep, practical experience executing physical failure analysis on electromechanical systems (actuators, harnesses, sensors, PCBAs, battery management systems, and precision mechanical linkages). 

 Methodologies: Certified or expert practitioner in structured root cause analysis tools (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone/Ishikawa, Fault Tree Analysis, FMEA, Gauge R&R). 

 
 Preferred Qualifications 

 
 Advanced Degree: Master’s degree in Engineering Management or an Engineering discipline. 

 Certifications: Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE), or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. 

 Domain Experience: Experience managing field reliability for autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robotics, or safety-critical industrial equipment. 

 Systems Exposure: Familiarity firmware diagnostic tools, and telemetry data analytics for remote fleet diagnostics. 

 
 Work Environment & Travel 

 
 Position is based out of our Salem, OR facility with regular access to testing labs, service centers, and assembly lines. 

 Occasional travel (up to 20%) to customer sites, field test locations, or primary suppliers may be required to investigate critical quality escapes. 

 
 
 Location 

 
 This is an onsite position at our Salem, OR office. 

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $162,000 — $210,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

records.title: Director, Workplace Operations
records.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

 OUR MISSION 

 True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

 OUR VALUES 

 
 Be the offset.   We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

 What would it take?  We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

 It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

 
 BENEFITS & PERKS *

 
 Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

 Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

 Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

 And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

 Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

 
 *Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

 YOUR MISSION 

 We are looking for an operations leader to take ownership of the everyday workplace operations at True Anomaly. From office management to culinary, janitorial to groundskeeping to beyond, you'll lead the teams and vendors that keep our workplaces running at a high standard. You own the full OPEX picture for our workplaces — managing to budget, forecasting with rigor, and always bringing cost-saving options to the table. You think in partnerships: working hand-in-hand with Real Estate to draw the line between Landlord scope and ours and with Development Planners to set long-term standards that drive operational efficiency downstream. You're a people leader at heart, a sharp cross-functional partner, and you'll flex to support services in our production areas when the mission calls for it. You take immense pride in your craft, and that pride shows up everywhere — in workplaces that run well, employees who feel taken care of, and an operations function that scales like a well-oiled machine.

 RESPONSIBILITIES 

 Lead and develop operations teams across multiple workplaces to support ongoing day-to-day needs, including office management, culinary/snacks, janitorial, groundskeeping, and related services. Define and own third-party vendor strategy across all service categories, ensuring consistent quality, reliability, and cost-effectiveness across the portfolio. Own the full OPEX budget for our workplaces, reporting out on forecast vs. budget regularly and surfacing cost-saving options. Partner hand-in-hand with the Real Estate team to define what work scope is the Landlord's responsibility versus ours. Partner hand-in-hand with Development Planners to develop long-term standards that support operational efficiencies downstream. Build scalable operations standards and processes that support growth into additional sites while maintaining a strong employee experience across all spaces. Support services within production areas as needed. Serve as a people leader and cross-functional partner inside and outside Facilities.

 QUALIFICATIONS 

 Required 

 
 7+ years of experience in workplace operations

 People management experience, including developing and growing teams

 Proven ability to own and manage a full OPEX budget, including forecasting and cost-saving identification

 Proven ability to define and manage third-party vendor strategy across multiple service categories

 Experience partnering with real estate on lease scope (Landlord vs. tenant responsibilities)

 Demonstrated ability to build scalable operations standards and processes

 Track record of delivering a strong employee experience across multiple sites

 Experience scaling a workplace operations function into new sites in a high-growth environment

 Familiarity with office management, culinary, janitorial, and groundskeeping service categories

 
 Nice to Have 

 
 Experience supporting secure environments

 Experience supporting services within production or manufacturing areas

 
 OTHER 

 
 Work Location - This position will be onsite 4 to 5 days per week at our Long Beach, CA facility

 
 COMPENSATION 

 
 Base Salary: $145,000-$210,000

 Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

 
 Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education and experience. 
 To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

 To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice .

records.title: Head of Bedrock Operations Center
records.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.

This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.

The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operations Center Strategy & Build-out

 - Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales

 - Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists

 - Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types

 - Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity

Remote Assistance

 - Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority

 - Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams

 - Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators

 - Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time

Customer & Partner Support

 - Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering

 - Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment

 - Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes

 - Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health

Central Operations / Command & Control

 - Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site

 - Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing

 - Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review

 - Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms

Performance & Analytics

 - Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership

 - Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it

 - Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution

 - Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently

 - Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements

 - The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)

 - Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces

 - Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments

 - Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)

 - Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations

 - Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives

Preferred

 - Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining

 - Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems

 - Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry

 - Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products

 - Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools

 - Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones

 - Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

records.title: Director, Accounting – Manufacturing
records.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role
Crusoe is looking for a Director of Accounting to own accounting, cost accounting and financial reporting for its manufacturing business. You'll report to the Corporate Controller and lead a multi-site team of 8+ and act as the accounting partner to Manufacturing leadership. You'll also build the cost, inventory and control infrastructure the business needs as production grows to meet demand for Crusoe's AI infrastructure.



Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy

 - Lead, build and develop a team of 8+ across multiple manufacturing facilities. Set the team's structure, hiring plan and development path as the business grows.

 - Act as the primary finance partner to manufacturing leadership (operations, supply chain, engineering, quality and procurement). Turn plant and assembly metrics into financial insight and decisions.

 - Drive financial accountability across operations by setting cost targets, tracking performance and influencing decisions on capacity, make-vs-buy, sourcing and pricing.

 - Advise executive leadership on product and program margins, cost-reduction opportunities and the financial impact of design, material and process changes.

Cost Accounting & Inventory

 - Own the cost accounting framework, including standard cost methodology, the annual standard-setting process, overhead absorption and labor rates.

 - Set and oversee inventory accounting policy, including valuation, WIP, high-value long-lead components, reserves and excess/obsolete inventory. Own the cycle count and physical inventory programs across all sites.

 - Lead analysis of manufacturing variances (purchase price, usage, labor, overhead), yield and productivity. Turn the results into actionable cost-improvement initiatives.

 - Own new-product and new-program cost estimates and margin modeling in partnership with Engineering and Sales.

Close, Reporting & Controls

 - Be accountable for a timely, accurate month-end close for the manufacturing entity. Present results, key drivers and risks to the Controller, CAO and operations leadership.

 - Ensure US GAAP compliance and own the manufacturing control environment, building it out to a SOX-ready, audit-ready standard. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors on manufacturing and inventory matters.

 - Lead the manufacturing entity's annual budget and rolling forecasts, working with FP&A.

Systems & Scale

 - Act as the accounting owner for the ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, work orders, costing) and lead system improvements and implementations.

 - Design, document and continuously improve scalable processes, with a focus on automation, as new facilities and product lines come online.



Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting. CPA or CMA required.

 - 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 5+ years in manufacturing or cost accounting and 3+ years leading teams (including managers).

 - Proven ownership of standard costing, inventory valuation and variance analysis in a complex, multi-site manufacturing environment.

 - Deep experience with ERP manufacturing modules (BOMs, routings, job and work-order costing). ERP implementation experience is a plus.

 - Experience with complex inventory, such as WIP, engineered-to-order or high-value long-lead components.

 - Strong knowledge of US GAAP and internal controls. SOX, public-company or Big 4 experience is a plus.

 - Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills.

 - High operational credibility: comfortable on the factory floor and able to influence senior operations and engineering leaders.

 - Track record of scaling teams, processes and systems in a high-growth environment.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $185,000 - $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

records.title: Head of Quality Assurance Operations
records.description:
ABOUT DAVID AI

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.




ABOUT OUR DATA OPERATIONS TEAM

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale. This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.



ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Head of Quality Assurance Operations, you'll own quality for every dataset David AI ships including but not limited to conversational, TTS, and transcription data, and manage David AI’s relationships with the global contingent workforce, comprising independent contractors and vendor-supplied contributors. You'll report to the Head of Operations and be located in the US.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own the quality bar across all data ops, including quality standards, calibration, consistency and on-time delivery of datasets

 - Design the quality review structure, organized by language and region, so every dataset gets consistent quality coverage

 - Audit and review the quality of delivered work product across languages, keeping quality benchmarks consistent globally

 - Run quality in languages you don't speak through deliverables from native-speaker and cross-language gold sets

 - Plan capacity against production ramps and own contingent workforce sourcing across many countries, ensuring each engagement is structured and classified correctly under local law

 - Build and own dashboards for quality, throughput, and cost efficiency

 - Manage David AI’s relationships with staffing vendors, service providers, and employer-of-record partners
 


YOUR BACKGROUND LOOKS LIKE

 - 7 to 10+ years in operations, including 3+ in senior leadership roles

 - You've run quality operations for large contingent workforce networks across multiple countries

 - You've owned quality at scale, across calibration, capacity planning, and spend efficiency

 - You built the system yourself, from tooling to contingent workforce sourcing at scale

 - Speech, audio, or linguistic data experience is a strong plus




BENEFITS

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Top-notch health, dental, and vision coverage with 100% coverage for most plans.

 - FSA & HSA access.

 - 401k access.

 - Meals 2x daily through DoorDash + snacks and beverages available at the office.

 - Unlimited company-sponsored Barry's classes.
 
 


VISAS

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B transfers, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on STEM OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

records.title: Staff Engineer, Manufacturing
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Job Description:

As a Staff Manufacturing Engineer, you’ll take ownership of critical manufacturing processes across multiple programs, leading initiatives to increase throughput, reduce costs, and scale our operations. You’ll be instrumental in building out the infrastructure for a new production line supporting a next-generation jet, including selecting and deploying capital equipment, implementing hardware and software tools, and establishing robust production systems. Working across engineering, supply chain, and production, you’ll ensure smooth integration of new technologies and provide mentorship to other engineers. This role is ideal for someone who thrives on cross-functional impact, technical leadership, and factory-scale execution. 

What You'll Do: 

 - 

 - Act as a technical leader across programs, owning the design and optimization of high-impact manufacturing processes. 

 - Drive the scale-up of our flagship product line, balancing throughput, quality, and cost. 

 - Lead the manufacturing engineering effort for launching a new production line for a larger and more capable jet. 

 - Scope and deploy critical production infrastructure, including manufacturing equipment, tooling, and hardware/software systems. 

 - Engage with vendors to source and integrate capital equipment, production tools, and automation systems. 

 - Mentor engineers and production personnel to build organizational capability and technical depth. 

 - Champion cross-functional initiatives that standardize and improve manufacturing performance at scale. 

Required Qualifications: 

 - 

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or relevant experience

 - 7+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, with a focus in rapid growth environments

 - Experience in owning the scale of production processes in a startup or rapid-growth environment.

 - Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, including machining, composites, avionics and/or assembly.

 - Experience with process improvement methodologies, such as Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma.

 - Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

 - 

 - Knowledge of quality standards, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001.

 - Proficiency in CAD software

 - Familiarity with advanced manufacturing technologies, such as additive manufacturing or automation systems.

 - Knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and data-driven decision-making in a manufacturing context.

 - Hands-on experience with manufacturing equipment and tooling design.

 - Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines.

#LI-JM1

#LD

 

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

 

###

 

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Join a high-impact quality engineering team supporting next-generation autonomous systems deployed in demanding operational environments. This role works closely with engineering, manufacturing, test, and field operations teams to identify product quality issues, drive root cause investigations, and improve system reliability across the product lifecycle. You will serve as a key link between field performance and engineering execution by translating operational issues into measurable product improvements.

We are seeking a Field Quality Engineer with experience supporting complex hardware systems in aerospace, defense, robotics, or related industries, including failure analysis, corrective actions, reliability tracking, and cross-functional problem solving.

What you'll do:

 - 

 - Investigate field-reported issues and drive root cause analysis across hardware, software, and integrated systems

 - Partner with engineering, manufacturing, and test teams to implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA)

 - Analyze reliability and performance trends to identify systemic quality issues and improve product robustness

 - Support validation, troubleshooting, and failure reproduction efforts for fielded systems

 - Develop quality metrics, reporting, and tracking tools to improve visibility into field performance and defect trends

 - Coordinate issue resolution across cross-functional teams while ensuring timely communication and closure

Required qualifications:

 - 

 - 5+ years of experience in quality engineering, field engineering, systems integration, manufacturing quality, or related technical roles

 - Strong experience with root cause analysis, failure investigation, and corrective action implementation in complex hardware environments

 - Ability to diagnose system-level issues across mechanical, electrical, and software interfaces

 - Experience analyzing reliability data, defect trends, and operational performance metrics

 - Strong communication and organizational skills with the ability to coordinate across engineering and operations teams

 - Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in fast-paced development and operational environments

Preferred qualifications:

 - 

 - Experience supporting aerospace, defense, robotics, or autonomous systems programs

 - Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, or regulated engineering environments

 - Experience with environmental testing, system validation, or field operations support

 - Experience using data analysis and reporting tools such as Python, SQL, Jira, Power BI, or Tableau

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality – Development Programs (R5315)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.

The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.

This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.

What you'll do:

 - Development Quality Leadership

 - Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.

 - Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.

 - Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.

 - Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.

 - Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.

 - Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.

Design & Configuration Quality

 - Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.

 - Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.

 - Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.

 - Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.

 - Support requirements verification and validation planning.

 - Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.

Risk Management & Reliability

 - Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.

 - Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.

 - Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.

 - Support reliability growth planning and execution.

 - Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.

Verification, Validation & Test Quality

 - Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.

 - Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.

 - Support qualification and certification efforts.

 - Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.

Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management

 - Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.

 - Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.

 - Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.

 - Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.

 - Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.

Production Readiness & Industrialization

 - Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.

 - Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.

 - Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.

 - Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.

 - Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.

Quality Management System

 - Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.

 - Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.

 - Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.

 - Support internal and external audits as required.

 - Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.

Leadership & Team Development

 - Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.

 - Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.

 - Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.

 - Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.

 - Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.

 - 10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.

 - 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.

 - Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.

 - Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.

 - Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.

 - Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.

 - Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

Preferred qualifications:

 - Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.

 - Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.

 - Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.

 - Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.

 - Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Job Description:

The Senior Air Vehicle Operator (AVO) – Deployment Operations is responsible for executing and leading V-BAT flight operations in support of DoD and foreign customers in both land-based and maritime OCONUS environments. This is an operationally focused role requiring strong aviation judgment, disciplined execution, and the ability to lead small teams in austere and high-visibility conditions. 

 

The Senior AVO is responsible for leading mission planning activities, performing comprehensive risk assessments, delivering pre-mission briefings, executing flight operations, and conducting structured post-flight debriefs. This role includes conducting Functional Check Flights (FCFs) and system validation as required, ensuring aircraft configuration control and logbook accuracy, coordinating with maintenance to sustain fleet readiness, and supporting overall operational discipline. The Senior AVO will mentor junior operators, serve as the on-site operational representative to customers, and travel extensively in support of deployments. 

 

This is not an entry-level flight operations role. The ideal candidate brings strong aviation fundamentals, disciplined cockpit habits, and mature operational decision-making. They must be comfortable leading deployments, briefing customers, managing risk in dynamic environments, and maintaining professionalism in high-visibility settings. The Senior AVO must balance mission execution with customer satisfaction while upholding the highest standards of safety, compliance, and operational excellence. 

Required Qualifications:

 - Minimum of 2000 documented unmanned flight hours or 1000 manned flight hours 

 - Demonstrated instructor experience (manned or unmanned aviation)  

 - FAA Private Pilot License (PPL)  

 - FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and maintain an FAA Class II Medical Certificate 

 - Ability to obtain and hold a Secret DoD security clearance 

 - Ability to pass background, drug screening, and customer-required medical/dental screenings 

 - Willingness to travel up to 50–75% in support of deployments 

 - Ability to lead and operate independently in small teams under austere conditions 

 - Strong aviation judgment, decision-making, and risk management skills 

Preferred Qualifications

 - FAA Instrument Rating and/or Commercial Pilot License  

 - Experience operating as aircrew on manned aircraft

records.title: Staff Engineer, Quality (R5512)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

At Shield AI, we’re building advanced autonomous aircraft that are redefining what is possible, and we are looking for a Staff Quality Engineer to help ensure our products meet the highest standards of performance, reliability, and safety. In this role, you will lead quality initiatives across the product lifecycle, driving improvements from early design and new product introduction through full-rate production.

 

You will be responsible for developing and maintaining robust quality systems in alignment with AS9100 standards, leading root cause investigations and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions. You will partner closely with engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to identify risks, improve process capability, and ensure consistent product quality. Your work will include supporting NPI efforts, establishing control plans and inspection strategies, and using data-driven methods to monitor and improve manufacturing performance.


As a Staff Quality Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping quality strategy, mentoring team members, and influencing cross-functional decisions without direct authority. This is an opportunity to work hands on with next generation aerospace technology and contribute directly to the delivery of highly reliable autonomous systems that will define the future of aviation.

Required qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience)

 - 5+ years of experience in Quality, Manufacturing, or Process Engineering roles

 - Demonstrated experience leading root cause analysis and implementing effective corrective and preventive actions (RCA/CAPA)

 - Strong knowledge of quality systems and standards (AS9100 or similar)

 - Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI) and scaling production in a manufacturing environment

 - Proficiency in statistical analysis and process control methods (SPC, capability analysis, etc.)

 - Proven ability to work cross-functionally and influence engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams

Preferred qualifications:

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Lean Six Sigma certification, or equivalent

 - Knowledge of design for quality principles, including DFMEA, tolerance analysis, and design reviews

 - Experience working with quality and manufacturing systems (QMS, MES, PLM) and data analysis tools

 - Familiarity with advanced inspection or test methods (metrology, NDT, automated inspection, etc.)

records.title: Senior Staff Engineer, ML Ops (R4941)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

 

Shield AI builds autonomy systems for defense applications, including air, maritime, and space platforms operating in complex and contested environments. 

We are building the AI Factory Reference Architecture, a Kubernetes-native platform for developing, training, evaluating, and deploying next-generation AI systems.

The AI Factory serves two purposes. Internally, it powers autonomy development across Hivemind and other AI programs. Externally, it becomes the reference architecture deployed into customer environments, spanning commercial cloud, on-premise infrastructure, sovereign deployments, and fully air-gapped systems.

We are looking for a Senior Staff Engineer to help define and build this platform. You will partner closely with ML researchers, platform engineers, and autonomy teams to deliver an exceptional developer experience for training and deploying modern AI models.

Success in this role requires balancing researcher productivity, platform simplicity, operational excellence, and long-term maintainability. You will work hands-on across the stack, helping shape both the platform architecture and its implementation while staying closely aligned with the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem. 

What you'll do:

 - 

 - AI Platform Development: Lead the design and implementation of the AI Factory Reference Architecture, delivering a Kubernetes-native platform for AI development, distributed training, simulation, evaluation, and deployment.

 - AI Research Enablement: Partner directly with ML researchers to understand evolving training workflows and ensure the platform supports state-of-the-art AI frameworks, foundation model development, reinforcement learning, distributed training, and emerging research workflows.

 - Developer Experience: Design self-service AI development workflows that enable engineers to move seamlessly from local experimentation to large-scale distributed execution using familiar open source tools and frameworks.

 - Distributed AI Infrastructure: Build the infrastructure required to support distributed training, simulation, inference, and reinforcement learning workloads. Evaluate and integrate orchestration, scheduling, and resource management technologies to maximize scalability and developer productivity.

 - Compute Platform: Design and optimize shared GPU infrastructure across cloud and on-premises environments. Improve resource utilization, scheduling efficiency, storage, networking, observability, and overall platform reliability.

 - Data & Model Lifecycle: Build platform capabilities that enable dataset management, experiment tracking, artifact management, model versioning, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous model improvement.

 - Platform Distribution: Develop repeatable deployment and lifecycle management solutions using Infrastructure as Code and modern platform engineering practices. Support commercial cloud, customer-managed infrastructure, sovereign environments, and fully air-gapped deployments.

 - Technology Leadership: Evaluate emerging AI infrastructure technologies and establish architectural patterns that balance scalability, performance, maintainability, and developer experience.

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with AI researchers, autonomy teams, infrastructure engineers, and product teams to ensure the platform evolves alongside customer needs and advances in AI.

Key Outcomes:

 - 

 - Engineers move from idea to distributed training in hours instead of days.

 - High GPU utilization through efficient scheduling with KAI on Kubernetes.

 - Researchers use modern AI tooling without unnecessary platform friction.

 - AI Workspaces become the standard development environment across autonomy programs.

 - Training, simulation, evaluation, and deployment operate as a unified platform.

 - The AI Factory Reference Architecture can be deployed consistently across cloud, on-premise, and air-gapped environments.

 - Platform capabilities are reusable across multiple autonomy programs and customer deployments.

Required qualifications:

 - 

 - Experience building Kubernetes-native AI or MLOps platforms supporting distributed machine learning workloads.

 - Deep understanding of modern AI training frameworks, including PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers and distributed training techniques.

 - Experience operating GPU-accelerated infrastructure and distributed training systems.

 - Strong understanding of Kubernetes, Linux, networking, security, storage, and distributed systems.

 - Experience with GPU scheduling concepts and large-scale AI workloads.

 - Experience packaging and deploying cloud-native infrastructure using Terraform and Helm.

 - Strong software engineering skills in Python and Golang and modern cloud-native technologies.

 - Experience collaborating closely with ML researchers to translate research workflows into scalable platform capabilities.

Preferred qualifications:

 - 

 - Experience with Ray or other distributed AI orchestration frameworks.

 - Experience with KAI, Slurm or other GPU scheduling technologies.

 - Experience supporting reinforcement learning, simulation-driven training, robotics, or autonomy workloads.

 - Experience deploying and optimizing AI models for edge hardware.

 - Experience designing infrastructure for classified, sovereign, or air-gapped environments.

 - Experience with observability technologies such as OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, and Grafana.

 - Experience contributing to or maintaining open-source infrastructure projects.

Why Join Us

 - The AI Factory is the foundation for how Shield AI develops and deploys autonomy.
 
 As a Senior Staff Engineer, you will help build the reference architecture used internally by our engineering teams and delivered to customers building their own AI capabilities. Your work will directly impact how quickly researchers can iterate, how efficiently compute resources are utilized, and how AI systems move from experimentation to operational deployment.
 
 This is an opportunity to work at the intersection of modern AI, distributed systems, Kubernetes, and defense, building a platform that enables the next generation of autonomy systems while leveraging the best of the open-source AI ecosystem.

records.title: Staff Engineer, Integration Advance Manufacturing (R5187)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We are seeking a highly cross-functional Staff Integration Advance Manufacturing Engineer to lead final system integration and production readiness activities for complex aerospace and defense platforms. This role is responsible for ensuring successful integration of electrical, mechanical, propulsion, and mission systems into complete operational vehicles and assemblies. 

The ideal candidate has broad multidisciplinary manufacturing experience and thrives in highly integrated production environments. 

What you'll do:

 - 

 - Lead manufacturing integration activities across electrical, mechanical, propulsion, and vehicle systems  

 - Develop and optimize final assembly and integration processes  

 - Coordinate system-level builds, integration sequencing, and production flow planning  

 - Partner with design engineering to improve manufacturability, reliability, testability, and producibility 

 - Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions for integration and assembly issues 

 - Develop work instructions, quality standards, and inspection methods  

 - Lead DFM/DFA reviews and transition new products into manufacturing 

 - Support system integration, validation, and troubleshooting activities 

 - Define manufacturing standards, process controls, and acceptance criteria 

 - Support failure analysis and reliability improvement initiatives 

 - Collaborate with production, quality, supply chain, and test engineering teams 

 - Mentor junior manufacturing engineers 

Tools & skills:

 - 

 - MES & QMS systems,

 - 3DEXPERIENCE / Teamcenter (PLM) systems

 - Supplier manufacturing processes

 - 5S/visual management

 - Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). 

Required qualifications:

 - 

 - 7+ years of manufacturing engineering or systems integration experience  

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related technical field  

 - Experience in prototype manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment. 

 - Experience with:  

 - Electrical and mechanical integration  

 - Production operations  

 - Manufacturing process development  

 - DFM/DFA principles  

 - Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities. 

 - Knowledge of manufacturing process development and production scaling  

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA principles  

 - Experience with root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies  

Preferred qualifications;

 - 

 - Aerospace or defense integration experience  

 - Experience supporting autonomous systems, UAVs, or advanced mobility platforms  

 - Familiarity with low-rate initial production (LRIP) and production scaling  

 - Experience with factory integration and manufacturing line design  

 - Experience with ERP/MES systems and manufacturing data analysis 

 - Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines 

 - Knowledge of quality standards, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001 

 - Proficiency in CAD software 

#LI-JM1

#LD

 

Full-time regular employee offer package:

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

 

###

 

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.
